correctness.rationale: Cycle-space reduction leaves a single winding H on the prism, and every closed walk with winding w uses at least n|w| edges. The published finite-graph CCA/GHM cycle-mean theorem gives rates |H|/n and |H|/(3n); the exact three-to-one GHM comparison follows from a verified coboundary. The explicit nine-state transfer counts the closed rung sequences and their H. A rational characteristic-polynomial computation verifies the flat count, and the positive shift-invariant Perron block gives a Gaussian variance \(\sigma^2=5/4-19\sqrt{33}/132\). Self-loops and a winding-three directed cycle show that precisely three peripheral Fourier phases contribute to the local-limit coefficient. Three supplied independent scripts cover exact transfer \(3\le n\le12\), direct CCA/GHM orbit evolution for all flat colorings at \(n=3,4,5\), and rational algebra. Finite experiments do not replace spectral proof.

value.rationale: Local vanishing square-circulation is a natural defect test for finite excitable media; the circular ladder has a single global topological obstruction not seen by this local test. The theorem gives the exact population of locally defect-free initial states, their full computable winding distribution, and the nontrivial probability law that almost all such states remain active but only at order \(n^{-1/2}\). This is a substantive infinite-family distinction between local charge and global activity, not merely a generic cycle criterion, and the precise probability answers a motivated network dynamical question.
